synopsis: MathWorks offers commercial MATLAB/Simulink, Offroad Autonomy Library and RoadRunner products with annual or perpetual per-product licensing; the latest release found was R2026b, the second 2026 release [f15877, f8963, f16239]. Its off-road evidence includes shipped excavator, backhoe and haul-truck examples and a Volvo CE human-in-the-loop excavator simulator, with dynamics, controller and sensor models available across the stack [f8285, f15879, f8599, f8960]. On 14 April 2026, IDIADA and MathWorks demonstrated closed-loop frontal AEB virtual-to-physical correlation for on-road cars using proving-ground tests and ISO 18571 metrics, but this did not establish a vehicle rating, and capability-building time was not found [f1761, f1762, f1271, f1763]. For heavy off-road braking, important gaps remain: high-fidelity soil deformation and sensor degradation require other models or custom work, RoadRunner needs custom work-site semantics, and independent validation of the complete automatic-braking stack was not found [f8394, f8607, f8395]. Pricing requires a quote; an unofficial January 2024 list gives indicative annual/perpetual prices of 980/3,920 for MATLAB, 1,480/5,920 for Simulink, 4,680/9,360 for RoadRunner and 3,400/13,600 for RoadRunner Scenario, all presumed US dollars rather than confirmed current prices [f8962, f16142, f16143, f16144, f16145].
